decisions.reason: A flagship reference electrometer at the core of the firm's dosimetry competence, featured on the home page for two years, clearly meets aspirations and calls for no search for alternatives.

The risk management software builds on the established QA offer and keeps a dedicated page; the firm's slack lets it carry a software product whose results are still uncertain while it supports the convergence strategy.
The CT phantom is a natural extension into imaging QA, fits the firm's resources, and is too new to have fallen below aspiration.
The mammography phantom is distant from the core and somewhat redundant with Product E, but it is only a year on the market and sits within the imaging QA push, so slack allows it to be kept for now.

The full field mammography phantom overlaps with D and is distant from the core, making it a candidate for consolidation if results disappoint, but it is too early for problemistic search to trigger dropping it.
This flagship imaging QA instrument line embodies the firm's strategic direction and will be kept and developed further.
